solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sacks returned for final part of letters

indicators.note: returned means the word for sacking is read backwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them, so sacks means fires

explanation.surface: Someone sends back sacks, perhaps of mail, in exchange for the last bit of the letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacks' is a verb here: the boss fires people.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small finishing stroke at the end of a printed letter's line.

clue.text: Dish for a European spread is in character, mostly

parts.note: a span is a spread or extent
at home means in, as in 'is he in?'

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A recipe for a European dish involving a spread that is somehow in character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the final R from LETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish omelette, with potato and onion, is the national egg dish of Spain, so a dish for a Spaniard.

clue.text: Right to give out pardon

parts.note: to emit is to give out, as of light or sound

explanation.surface: A claim that someone has the right to grant a pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit a sin or penalty is to cancel it, which is a formal sense of forgiving it.

clue.text: What's established during a number of Christmases?

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: five is a number
EST is the abbreviation for established, seen on shop signs

explanation.surface: A quiz question about which tradition has held over several Christmases.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive means relating to a feast or celebration, above all the Christmas season.

clue.text: Weaving carpet and matting would surely defeat me

indicators.note: weaving suggests threads being worked into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone weaving a carpet and a mat says the work would beat them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a soft mat would muffle the metal taps on the shoes, defeating the performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing needs a hard floor for the shoe plates to click on, so matting would thwart this performer.

clue.text: Weak object loses its end

indicators.note: loses its end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A feeble item that has lost its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin can mean weak or feeble, as in a thin excuse or a thin voice.

clue.text: Small flat pastry with fruit? Sin coming up!

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
a date is a fruit

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A baker's flat pastry with fruit, then a guilty cry as temptation strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' seems to describe pastry but means an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small second home, often a flat kept in a city.

clue.text: Strangely genial Conservative is exceptionally kind

indicators.note: strangely means the letters are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A surprisingly pleasant Tory turns out to be very kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic describes someone as good and gentle as an angel, which is extreme kindness.

clue.text: Reason for action about America? No, it's over

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
USA is America

indicators.note: over means the words are turned back to front

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether America is the reason for acting, and is told the matter is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses NO IT to give TION; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Causation is the bringing about of an effect, what makes something happen.

clue.text: Film a red car for novel adaptation outside suspect café in Oxford location

indicators.note: outside means the first jumble wraps around the second one
a novel adaptation reworks the material freshly, so these letters are rearranged
suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Filming an adaptation of a novel with a red car outside a dodgy café somewhere in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like the start of the scene but is anagram fodder; 'outside' wraps the 'novel adaptation' of FILM A RED CAR around the 'suspect' jumble of CAFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Radcliffe Camera is a domed eighteenth-century library building, a famous Oxford landmark.

clue.text: Peace created by fog and frost by a river

parts.note: mist is a light fog
ice is frozen water, like frost

explanation.surface: Peace comes about thanks to winter weather by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a river' places A and R before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is an agreed truce that ends fighting, so a form of peace.

clue.text: This trailer is a water container

definitions.meaning: a trailing plant of the squash family that sprawls along the ground
the hard dried shell of that fruit, hollowed out to hold water

explanation.surface: A trailer, apparently a vehicle, turns out to be a water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' suggests a vehicle; here it is a plant that trails.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant trails along the ground, and its dried hollow fruit serves as a flask or bottle.

clue.text: Just know Eskimos will have little time inside

indicators.note: will have, with inside, says one piece holds the other within it
inside completes the instruction that one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Inuit are the Arctic people once called Eskimos
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A claim that Arctic people simply know things and have little time for indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to grasp something by instinct, without reasoning it out.

clue.text: Way for London to lose its attraction and shopping centre

parts.note: to pall is to become dull or tiresome
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A London street that has lost its appeal and become a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall Mall is a well-known street in central London, home to many gentlemen's clubs.

clue.text: Prophet's hurrying to give an example of joint endeavour

parts.note: Job is an Old Testament figure, here with the possessive 's
haring means running fast like a hare

explanation.surface: A prophet rushes about to show how people can work together.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people splitting one post between them is a shared working arrangement.

clue.text: Round campanula flower turned back in present flowering plant

indicators.note: in means one piece goes within the other

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

indicators.note: turned back means these pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: O is round in shape
the campanula is the bellflower, so its flower is a bell

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a bell-shaped bloom bending back in a showy plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' makes LLEBO, which goes inside HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hellebore, such as the Christmas rose, is a winter-flowering perennial.

clue.text: Member misses deadline to vote through law

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
someone who misses a deadline is late

explanation.surface: An MP misses the cutoff for voting a bill into law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which a parliament does by voting them in.

clue.text: Bluff chap

definitions.meaning: as a noun, a steep headland or bank
a man's given name, as for the singer Richard

explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep rock face, and it is also a common boy's name.

clue.text: Will possibly sounds like a small child

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is said aloud for its twin in sound

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A will may be read out, and sounds like a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Might expresses possibility, a weaker form of will, as in it might rain.

clue.text: Challenged traveller in space series killing star king and queen

indicators.note: killing means getting rid of the named word

parts.note: Star Trek is the space TV series
the word star is removed as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is the abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A space TV series kills off its star, a king and a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A trekker makes a long, arduous journey, often on foot, so a traveller facing challenges.

clue.text: Girl group with European dance number

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A girl band with a European member performs a dance track.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarabande is a slow, stately Spanish dance, and a piece of music written for it.

clue.text: Girl is cross over ending of benefit

parts.note: to bridge a gap is to cross over it

indicators.note: ending of means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A girl is angry about benefits ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry but means to span.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget is a girl's name.

clue.text: Large wild agaves adjacent to sierra resort

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Big untamed agave plants grow beside a mountain range near a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas in Nevada is a desert gambling and entertainment resort city.

clue.text: Man and woman creating fine woollen cloth

parts.note: Vic is a man's name
Una is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A couple are making a fine woollen fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicuna is a soft, costly fabric woven from the wool of the Andean animal of that name.

clue.text: Merged group of four banks in the City

indicators.note: a run of letters straddling the merged words is taken from them

explanation.surface: Four banks merge in the City of London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial centre; here any city will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means of or in a town or city, as opposed to rural.

clue.text: Run in Oscar Wilde, perhaps for a court order

indicators.note: in means the letter goes within the word

parts.note: Oscar Wilde is an example of a wit, a clever joker
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde runs into trouble and is served with a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilde famously faced the courts, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written command issued by a court.

clue.text: Way to change one's view when queen enters

indicators.note: enters means the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: to tack is to change course or approach
R, for Regina, means queen

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind once the queen comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a path or route, so a way.

clue.text: Prickly, good for temperature, as most desert crops are

indicators.note: for means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: irritable means touchy or prickly

explanation.surface: Prickly plants, good when the heat is on, describe desert crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for temperature' puts G where IRRITABLE has its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert crops need artificial watering, so they are grown on land that can be watered by channels.

clue.text: Some rowing about agreement with king's order to forces

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the others

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew, part of the rowing world
yes is a word of agreement
R, for Rex, means king

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is in agreement with the king's command to the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is a parade-ground command for soldiers to turn their heads to the right.

clue.text: Fail with a Japanese poem

parts.note: to tank is to fail badly

explanation.surface: A Japanese poem that flops.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanka is a short Japanese verse form of five lines and thirty-one syllables.
